Class

Precalculus

Explore Precalculus through jumps, wheels and trail profiles: rotation is trigonometry, speed off a lip is a vector, and a rolling wheel traces a parametric curve.

9 units · 41 topics · activities in development

Units

  1. Unit 1 Advanced Functions 5 topics

    1. Function Transformations

      Combine shifts, stretches and reflections of any parent function.

      • Recognize the parent functions
      • Apply combinations of transformations
      • Write a transformed function from a graph
      Activities in development

    2. Polynomial Functions

      Review polynomial functions, their graphs and modeling uses.

      • Identify degree, leading coefficient and zeros
      • Model data with polynomial functions
      • Solve polynomial inequalities
      Activities in development

    3. Rational Functions

      Recognize rational functions and their domains as a family of functions.

      • Identify rational functions
      • Find domains of rational functions
      • Use rational functions in models
      Activities in development

    4. Inverse Functions

      Find inverses, restrict domains, and connect graphs by reflection in y = x.

      • Find inverses algebraically
      • Restrict a domain so an inverse exists
      • Graph inverses
      Activities in development

    5. Composition of Functions

      Compose and decompose functions, with domains.

      • Compose functions and find the domain
      • Decompose functions
      • Build chained real-world models
      Activities in development
  2. Unit 2 Polynomial and Rational Functions 5 topics

    1. Polynomial Behavior

      Increasing and decreasing intervals, local extrema and turning points.

      • Find increasing and decreasing intervals
      • Estimate local maxima and minima
      • Sketch polynomial functions
      Activities in development

    2. Roots and Zeros

      Find all zeros, real and complex, and use them to factor.

      • Find all zeros of a polynomial
      • Find complex zeros and conjugate pairs
      • Write a polynomial in factored form
      Activities in development

    3. End Behavior

      Describe what a function does as x → ±∞.

      • Describe polynomial end behavior
      • Describe rational end behavior
      • Write end behavior with limit notation
      Activities in development

    4. Rational Functions

      Analyze and graph rational functions fully.

      • Find intercepts, holes and asymptotes
      • Graph rational functions
      • Solve rational inequalities
      Activities in development

    5. Asymptotes

      Vertical, horizontal and oblique asymptotes, and behavior near them.

      • Find all asymptotes
      • Describe behavior near a vertical asymptote
      • Decide whether a graph crosses its horizontal asymptote
      Activities in development
  3. Unit 3 Exponential and Logarithmic Functions 4 topics

    1. Exponential Models

      Build and use exponential models, including continuous growth.

      • Build exponential models from data
      • Use continuous growth models
      • Interpret parameters in context
      Activities in development

    2. Logarithmic Models

      Use logarithmic functions to model and linearize data.

      • Build logarithmic models
      • Linearize exponential data with logarithms
      • Work with logarithmic scales
      Activities in development

    3. Logarithmic Properties

      Use log properties to solve equations.

      • Apply product, quotient and power properties
      • Solve exponential equations
      • Solve logarithmic equations
      Activities in development

    4. Applications

      Apply exponential and logarithmic models to growth, decay and cooling.

      • Solve growth and decay problems
      • Use Newton’s law of cooling
      • Interpret logistic growth
      Activities in development
  4. Unit 4 Trigonometry 5 topics

    1. Degrees and Radians

      Measure angles in radians and convert between units.

      • Convert between degrees and radians
      • Use s = rθ
      • Find angular and linear speed
      Activities in development

    2. Unit Circle

      Define sine and cosine as coordinates on the unit circle.

      • Find exact values on the unit circle
      • Use reference angles
      • Determine signs by quadrant
      Activities in development

    3. Sine, Cosine, and Tangent

      The six trigonometric functions of any angle.

      • Evaluate all six trigonometric functions
      • Find exact values for special angles
      • Use a calculator in degree and radian mode
      Activities in development

    4. Right Triangle Trigonometry

      SOH-CAH-TOA: find sides and angles of right triangles.

      • Find missing sides with trig ratios
      • Find angles with inverse trig
      • Solve angle of elevation and depression problems
      Activities in development

    5. Trigonometric Identities

      Prove and use fundamental identities.

      • Use Pythagorean identities
      • Use sum and difference formulas
      • Use double-angle formulas
      Activities in development
  5. Unit 5 Trigonometric Functions 5 topics

    1. Graphing Sine and Cosine

      Graph y = a sin(b(x − h)) + k and y = a cos(b(x − h)) + k.

      • Graph sine and cosine
      • Use key points to sketch a period
      • Write an equation from a graph
      Activities in development

    2. Periodic Functions

      Recognize and model repeating behavior.

      • Identify periodic functions
      • Model periodic data
      • Graph tangent and the reciprocal functions
      Activities in development

    3. Amplitude and Period

      Find and interpret amplitude and period.

      • Find and interpret amplitude
      • Find and interpret period
      • Relate period and frequency
      Activities in development

    4. Phase Shifts

      Horizontal and vertical shifts of trig graphs.

      • Find phase shift
      • Find the midline
      • Graph with combined shifts
      Activities in development

    5. Inverse Trigonometric Functions

      Evaluate and graph inverse sine, cosine and tangent with restricted domains.

      • Evaluate inverse trig functions
      • Explain the restricted domains
      • Solve trigonometric equations
      Activities in development
  6. Unit 6 Trigonometric Applications 5 topics

    1. Law of Sines

      Solve non-right triangles with a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C, including the ambiguous case.

      • Use the law of sines
      • Handle the ambiguous SSA case
      • Solve applied problems
      Activities in development

    2. Law of Cosines

      c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C for any triangle.

      • Use the law of cosines
      • Find angles from three sides
      • Find triangle area with ½ab sin C
      Activities in development

    3. Solving Triangles

      Choose the right tool to find every side and angle.

      • Choose between right-triangle trig, sines and cosines
      • Solve triangles completely
      • Check that a solution is reasonable
      Activities in development

    4. Bearings and Angles

      Navigation with bearings.

      • Read and write bearings
      • Solve bearing problems with triangles
      • Plan a route with bearings
      Activities in development

    5. Applications of Trigonometry

      Heights, distances and angles in real situations.

      • Find heights and distances
      • Solve multi-step angle problems
      • Choose a trig model for a situation
      Activities in development
  7. Unit 7 Vectors 4 topics

    1. Vector Components

      Break a vector into horizontal and vertical parts.

      • Find horizontal and vertical components
      • Write vectors in component form
      • Interpret components in context
      Activities in development

    2. Vector Magnitude

      Find the length and direction of a vector.

      • Find magnitude
      • Find direction angle
      • Find unit vectors
      Activities in development

    3. Vector Addition

      Add and subtract vectors graphically and with components.

      • Add vectors graphically
      • Add vectors with components
      • Find a resultant
      Activities in development

    4. Direction and Velocity

      Use vectors for velocity and force problems.

      • Solve velocity problems
      • Solve force problems
      • Use the dot product to find angles
      Activities in development
  8. Unit 8 Parametric and Polar Functions 4 topics

    1. Parametric Equations

      Describe motion with x(t) and y(t).

      • Write parametric equations for motion
      • Eliminate the parameter
      • Model projectile motion parametrically
      Activities in development

    2. Parametric Graphs

      Graph parametric curves and read direction and timing.

      • Graph parametric curves
      • Show direction of motion
      • Describe the cycloid
      Activities in development

    3. Polar Coordinates

      Locate points with (r, θ) and convert to and from rectangular form.

      • Plot points in polar coordinates
      • Convert points between polar and rectangular
      • Convert equations between forms
      Activities in development

    4. Polar Graphs

      Graph circles, roses, cardioids and spirals.

      • Graph polar equations
      • Recognize roses, limaçons and cardioids
      • Use symmetry to graph
      Activities in development
  9. Unit 9 Sequences, Series, and Limits 4 topics

    1. Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences

      Rules, terms and recursive definitions.

      • Write explicit and recursive rules
      • Identify the type of sequence
      • Model with sequences
      Activities in development

    2. Series

      Sums of finite and infinite series; sigma notation.

      • Find finite sums
      • Find infinite geometric sums
      • Use sigma notation
      Activities in development

    3. Mathematical Limits

      What value a function approaches; one-sided limits and limits at infinity.

      • Estimate limits from tables and graphs
      • Find one-sided limits
      • Find limits at infinity
      Activities in development

    4. Introduction to Calculus Concepts

      Instantaneous rate of change and area under a curve.

      • Estimate instantaneous rate of change
      • Interpret the slope of a tangent line
      • Estimate area under a curve
      Activities in development
